svg.title: Anatomy of one Diary work block
svg.desc: A work block has six ordered fields: local identity and timestamp, exact prompts, an ordered plan, verified progress, journal lessons, and exactly one lifecycle status. Stable entry identifiers link a resumed copy to its paused source within the same Diary.

g.text: The block is the unit of continuity
One coherent piece of work, including its corrections — not one new block for every message.
1 · Identity + time
2 · Exact prompt
3 · Ordered plan
4 · Progress
5 · Journal + lessons
6 · Lifecycle status
Which record am I continuing?
What was actually requested?
What is the current order of work?
What is verified, and what remains?
What should the next self avoid?
What is the real state of the work?
Local block number · stable entry ID · timestamp · task identity
A resumed copy also names its source block and entry ID.
Original user text, preserved verbatim
Related corrections are appended with “+”; old requests remain visible.
Numbered steps in execution-priority order
A correction may replace this plan without erasing the prompt history.
Milestones · evidence · finished steps · next action
Write a checkpoint before switching direction or responding to a correction.
Misunderstanding → correction → next-self guidance
Store useful lessons, not a transcript of private model reasoning.
Working / Complete / Cancelled / Paused
Exactly one canonical stored tag. Unfinished work is never “complete.”
Ownership is outside the conversation's memory.
The surrounding Diary and scope metadata isolate the task. Numbers and resume links never cross Diaries.
